entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-v76p-62qx-wwq2: ImageSharp: Tiled fax TIFF: tile buffer sized by TileWidth but fax decompressor writes scanlines of ImageWidth — heap OOB write
entry.content:
ImageSharp: Tiled fax TIFF: tile buffer sized by TileWidth but fax decompressor writes scanlines of ImageWidth — heap OOB write

Aliases: CVE-2026-106118

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 3.2.0
  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 4.1.1

## Summary When decoding a tiled TIFF with fax compression (T4/T6/MH), `DecodeTilesChunky` allocates each tile buffer from **TileWidth** (`ceil(TileWidth*bpp/8)*TileLength` bytes) but constructs the fax decompressor with **frame.Width**: `TiffDecompressorsFactory` ignores the `isTiled/tileWidth/tileHeight` parameters entirely. The T4/T6/MH decompressors treat the full image width as the scanline length and advance (and really write, via read-modify-write bit ops) `frame.Width` bits per row, with no bounds check against the tile buffer. The very first tile therefore writes linearly out of bounds — about `ImageWidth/8` bytes per row × TileLength rows into a `TileWidth`-sized buffer. With ImageWidth=4,000,000, TileWidth=16, TileLength=16 this writes ~2 MB past a 32-byte buffer and kills the …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-wmxv-xphr-5c9g: ImageSharp: BigTIFF IFD count can keep a decoder thread in a non-progressing loop
entry.content:
ImageSharp: BigTIFF IFD count can keep a decoder thread in a non-progressing loop

Aliases: CVE-2026-106116

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 3.2.0
  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 4.1.2

### Summary `SixLabors.ImageSharp` 4.1.1 can spend an attacker-controlled duration decoding a small malformed BigTIFF. The BigTIFF IFD entry-count field is 64-bit. The reader iterates once per declared entry, but when fewer than 20 bytes remain for an entry, the entry read returns without advancing. A 24-byte input can therefore run billions of iterations without consuming input. One decoder invocation occupied one executing thread for more than five seconds in the tested environment. This report makes no worker-pool exhaustion claim. ### Affected package and versions - Package: `SixLabors.ImageSharp` (NuGet) - Affected range: `>= 2.0.0, <= 4.1.1` - Commit `0815358f9202a78bc7f3b83e19282dc3654b500f` corresponds to release **v4.1.1**. BigTIFF decoding and the unbounded `ReadValues64` lo…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j3p4-wp97-rph4: ImageSharp: HistogramEqualization uses an unvalidated luminance as an unchecked histogram index
entry.content:
ImageSharp: HistogramEqualization uses an unvalidated luminance as an unchecked histogram index

Aliases: CVE-2026-106113

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 3.2.0
  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 4.1.2

### Summary `SixLabors.ImageSharp` can terminate a process when an application decodes an attacker-supplied 32-bit floating-point TIFF as `Image<HalfVector4>` and applies `HistogramEqualization()`. An IEEE positive-infinity TIFF sample reaches a non-finite or otherwise out-of-range `HalfVector4` component, depending on the release. The histogram equalization path derives a luminance-based histogram index without validating that result, reaching an unsafe out-of-range access. This report covers `HistogramEqualization` only. It does not claim Adaptive Histogram Equalization or AutoLevel behavior. ### Affected package and versions - Package: `SixLabors.ImageSharp` (NuGet) - Affected range: `>= 2.0.0, <= 4.1.1` - Commit `0815358f9202a78bc7f3b83e19282dc3654b500f` corresponds to release **v4…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-gwg2-r3hj-4w44: ImageSharp: ICC CLUT parsing allocates from unvalidated channel and grid dimensions
entry.content:
ImageSharp: ICC CLUT parsing allocates from unvalidated channel and grid dimensions

Aliases: CVE-2026-106114

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 4.1.2
  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 3.2.0

### Summary A malformed embedded ICC profile can make ImageSharp allocate memory from attacker-controlled CLUT channel and grid dimensions before verifying that the declared CLUT values are present. In published v1 through v3 packages, the public lazy ICC parser allocates approximately 115 MB from the 200-byte test profile before rejecting the truncated tag. In published v4 packages, decoding with ICC conversion enabled requests an 860,934,420-byte managed float array from the same profile. ### Affected package and versions - Package: `SixLabors.ImageSharp` (NuGet) - Affected range: `>= 1.0.0-beta0001, <= 4.1.1` - Commit `0815358f9202a78bc7f3b83e19282dc3654b500f` corresponds to release **v4.1.1**. The parser defect is present from the first published NuGet prerelease, `1.0.0-beta0001`…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j9gm-c75j-xc9q: ImageSharp: TIFF CCITT T4 encoder can write past its compressed output buffer
entry.content:
ImageSharp: TIFF CCITT T4 encoder can write past its compressed output buffer

Aliases: CVE-2026-106110

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 3.2.0
  • SixLabors.ImageSharp — fixed in 4.1.2

### Summary ImageSharp's TIFF CCITT Group 3 (T4) encoder can write beyond its allocated compressed-data buffer when encoding narrow 1-bit images. The unchecked writes can corrupt process memory and terminate the process. This report concerns only the T4 `CcittGroup3Fax` encoder path. It replaces the prior, unrelated ICC content. ### Affected package and versions - Package: `SixLabors.ImageSharp` (NuGet) - Affected range: `>= 2.0.0, <= 4.1.1` - Commit `0815358f9202a78bc7f3b83e19282dc3654b500f` corresponds to release **v4.1.1**. The T4 encoder and its undersized buffer calculation first shipped in v2.0.0. The narrow-image exploit terminates published v2.0.0 and v4.1.1 while the same-height 64-pixel control succeeds on both. Every release through v4.1.1 retains the vulnerable allocation …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-px2c-r924-mwcc: Couchbase .NET SDK (client library) does not properly enable hostname verification for TLS certificates
entry.content:
Couchbase .NET SDK (client library) does not properly enable hostname verification for TLS certificates

Aliases: CVE-2025-49015

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • CouchbaseNetClient — fixed in 3.7.1

The Couchbase .NET SDK (client library) before 3.7.1 does not properly enable hostname verification for TLS certificates. In fact, the SDK was also using IP addresses instead of hostnames due to a configuration option that was incorrectly enabled by default.
